title: Faithful matrix realization and weight blocks for a central split torus
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed subgroups as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $H$ be an affine $F$-group scheme of finite type and let $T\subset H$ be a central closed subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$. Here $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$; central means commuting with all elements after every scalar extension. There exist a finite-dimensional nonzero $F$-vector space $V$, a closed-immersion homomorphism $\rho:H\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(V)$, and a decomposition $V=\bigoplus_{i=1}^s V_i$ with each $V_i\ne0$, such that each $V_i$ is $H$-stable and $T$ acts on $V_i$ through a character $\chi_i:T\to\mathbf G_m$. Explicitly, for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, $\rho_A(t)|_{V_i\otimes_F A}=\chi_i(t)\operatorname{id}$, and the action of $H(A)$ restricts to $V_i\otimes_F A$. The tuple of characters $(\chi_i):T\to\mathbf G_m^s$ is a closed immersion. Here $\operatorname{GL}(V)(A)=\operatorname{Aut}_A(V\otimes_F A)$, and a closed immersion of affine schemes is one induced by a surjection of coordinate algebras.

source.place: Theorem 4.9 and Corollary 4.10, printed p.87; Theorem 12.12, printed pp.234--235; Proposition 12.46(a), proof, printed p.246 (weight blocks and their centralizer)

proof.text: Put $C=F[H]$, with comultiplication $\Delta$, counit $\epsilon$, and antipode induced by the group operations. The affine-pair criterion [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], applied to $H\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ and the whole affine opens, says that $C$ is a finitely generated $F$-algebra. Choose finite algebra generators and adjoin $1$. Apply [lem-sfb-comodule-finite-subrepresentation] to the regular coaction $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_F C$ and this finite set. Its coassociativity and counit identities are the group identities. We obtain a finite-dimensional subspace $V\subset C$ containing $1$ and all generators, with $\Delta(V)\subset V\otimes_F C$. Since $\epsilon(1)=1$, $V\ne0$. Take a finite spanning list of $V$ as in [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] and discard each vector in the span of its predecessors. The retained list spans and is independent (a relation with nonzero last coefficient would contradict retention), hence is a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_N$, $N\ge1$, and write $\Delta(e_j)=\sum_i e_i\otimes a_{ij}$. The finite-subrepresentation node explicitly asserts that $V$ with this restricted coaction is again a rational module; its statement supplies both restricted coaction identities.

source.place: Theorem 4.9, printed p.87, first paragraph; finite-dimensional subcomodule supplied by Proposition 4.7, p.86; affine-pair criterion: Stacks Tag 01T2, morphisms.tex, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-hopf-coaction-linearization] with $E=F$ (trivial algebra coaction) and $M=V$. The coaction gives a $C$-linear automorphism of $V\otimes_F C$; evaluating along $g:C\to A$ gives the matrix $(g(a_{ij}))$ for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$. Its identity and composition laws give a homomorphism $\rho:H\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$. More explicitly, coassociativity and the counit give $\Delta(a_{ij})=\sum_k a_{ik}\otimes a_{kj}$ and $\epsilon(a_{ij})=\delta_{ij}$. The inverse supplied by the antipode makes $\det(a_{ij})$ a unit in $C$, so [def-sc-general-linear-group] gives the coordinate map $F[x_{ij},\det(x)^{-1}]\to C$, $x_{ij}\mapsto a_{ij}$. Its image contains $e_j=\sum_i\epsilon(e_i)a_{ij}$ by the left counit identity on $C$. Hence it contains $V$ and the chosen algebra generators of $C$, and is surjective. By the affine quotient meaning of closed immersion in the statement, $\rho$ is a closed immersion. This proves faithfulness scheme-theoretically, including for nonreduced $H$.

source.place: Remark 4.1 and equations (24)--(25), printed p.84; Theorem 4.9, printed p.87, counit calculation

proof.text:
Fix $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. We will refine $V$ successively by the $r$ coordinate factors. The following coefficient check makes each refinement $H$-stable. If $W\subset V$ is already $H$-stable, restrict one coordinate $\mathbf G_m\to T$ to $W$ and use [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] to write $W=\bigoplus_a W_a$ (finitely many nonzero integer weights). Fix an $F$-algebra $A$, $h\in H(A)$ and $w\in W_a\otimes_F A$, and write $\rho_A(h)w=\sum_b u_b$ with $u_b\in W_b\otimes_F A$. These base-changed summands form a direct sum: bases of the $W_b$ concatenate to a basis of $W$, and their coordinate maps extend by tensoring. Extend scalars to $B=A\otimes_F F[z,z^{-1}]$ and take the universal point $z\in\mathbf G_m(B)$ in the chosen coordinate. Centrality gives
$$\sum_b u_bz^b=z^a\sum_b u_b.$$
Apply the $A$-linear coefficient maps obtained by tensoring the $F$-linear coefficient maps of [def-weil-laurent-polynomial-ring] with $A$. They give $u_b=0$ for $b\ne a$. This works even for nonreduced $A$; the inclusion of constants has the retraction given by $z=1$. Thus $h$ preserves $W_a\otimes_F A$; applying the same calculation to $h^{-1}$ makes the restriction an automorphism. The restricted representation is a morphism: its matrix entries are the corresponding block entries of $\rho$, and its inverse is the corresponding block of $\rho(h^{-1})$.

source.place: Theorem 12.12 and Remark 12.13, printed pp.234--235; Proposition 12.46(a), proof, printed p.246, centralizer of the weight decomposition

proof.text: Induct on $j$, $0\le j\le r$: there is a finite direct sum into nonzero $H$-stable subspaces, each with an integer weight for each of the first $j$ coordinate factors. For $j=0$ the single summand is $V\ne0$ and the empty weight tuple has trivial character. Given the decomposition for $j$, apply [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] to factor $j+1$ on each summand and discard zero weight spaces. Step 3 proves that every refined space is $H$-stable, so the next coordinate action is defined on it; the first $j$ scalar actions retain their weights on every subspace. There are finitely many old summands and finitely many weights on each, so the refinement remains finite and direct, and still sums to $V$. After $r$ steps write the summands as $V_1,\ldots,V_s$. If $(a_{i1},\ldots,a_{ir})$ is the weight tuple of $V_i$, put $\chi_i(t_1,\ldots,t_r)=\prod_{j=1}^r t_j^{a_{ij}}$. This is a group-scheme character by the unit-valued functor description of $\mathbf G_m$ in [def-sc-gm-ga]. Every $t\in T(A)$ is the product of its $r$ coordinate points, so on $V_i\otimes_F A$ its action is $\chi_i(t)\operatorname{id}$. For $r=0$ the empty product gives the trivial character, and $s=1$.

source.place: Theorem 12.12 and Remark 12.13, printed pp.234--235: finite product version obtained here by induction from the existing one-factor theorem

proof.text:
Choose a basis within each nonzero $V_i$ and concatenate them. On $T$, the matrix entries of $\rho$ in this basis are either zero or $\chi_i$, each $\chi_i$ repeated $n_i=\dim_F V_i\ge1$ times; the determinant restricts to $\prod_i\chi_i^{n_i}$. The coordinate map $F[\operatorname{GL}(V)]\to F[T]$ is surjective: the first map to $C$ is surjective by step 2 and $C\to F[T]$ is surjective since $T\subset H$ is a closed subgroup. Changing basis does not change this, since conjugation and its inverse give inverse morphisms of $\operatorname{GL}(V)$. The presentation in [def-sc-general-linear-group] shows that this surjective map factors through the coordinate map
$$F[y_1^{\pm1},\ldots,y_s^{\pm1}]\longrightarrow F[T],\qquad y_i\longmapsto\chi_i,$$
by sending an entry in block $i$ on the diagonal to $y_i$, all other entries to zero, and $\det(x)^{-1}$ to $\prod_i y_i^{-n_i}$. Therefore this Laurent map is surjective too: every element of $F[T]$ lifts through the displayed factorization. It is exactly the coordinate map of $(\chi_i):T\to\mathbf G_m^s$, using [def-sc-gm-ga] and the algebra tensor-product universal property for the finite product. Thus the character tuple is a closed immersion. Positivity of the $n_i$ follows because zero summands were discarded; $V\ne0$ ensures $s\ge1$.

Constructed a faithful regular subrepresentation by matrix coefficients and the counit, proved H-stability by a universal Laurent-variable calculation, refined by induction on the split-torus rank, and proved the character tuple is a closed immersion by a surjective coordinate-algebra factorization. No new nodes, no statement changes, no Lean attachment.

lean.statement: theorem exists_faithful_weight_blocks {F : Type u} [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (H T : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) [IsAffine H.X.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType H.X.hom] [QuasiCompact H.X.hom] (iT : T ⟶ H) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme iT.hom.hom] (r : ℕ) (hsplit : Nonempty (T ≅ MultiplicativeType.splitTorus F r)) (hcentral : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra F A] (t : (Spec (.of A)).asOver (Spec (.of F)) ⟶ T.X) (h : (Spec (.of A)).asOver (Spec (.of F)) ⟶ H.X), Commute (t ≫ iT.hom.hom) h) : ∃ (N : ℕ) (_ : 0 < N) (ρ : H ⟶ Grp.mk (GeneralLinearGroup (ULift.{u} (Fin N)) F)) (s : ℕ) (V : Fin s → Submodule F (ULift.{u} (Fin N) → F)) (χ : Fin s → (T ⟶ Grp.mk (StandardGroupSchemes.multiplicative F))), IsClosedImmersion ρ.hom.hom.left ∧ DirectSum.IsInternal V ∧ (∀ i : Fin s, V i ≠ ⊥) ∧ (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra F A] (h : (Spec (.of A)).asOver (Spec (.of F)) ⟶ H.X) (i : Fin s) (v : A ⊗[F] (ULift.{u} (Fin N) → F)), v ∈ (V i).baseChange A → pointAction ρ.hom.hom A h v ∈ (V i).baseChange A) ∧ (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra F A] (t : (Spec (.of A)).asOver (Spec (.of F)) ⟶ T.X) (i : Fin s) (v : A ⊗[F] (ULift.{u} (Fin N) → F)), v ∈ (V i).baseChange A → pointAction ρ.hom.hom A (t ≫ iT.hom.hom) v = characterScalar (χ i) A t • v) ∧ IsClosedImmersion (Pi.lift (fun i : Fin s ↦ (χ i).hom.hom)).left
